children: Oil falls in early trade, weighed down by the International Energy Agency's announcement to release crude oil and diesel fuel. The IEA said Thursday that the volume of emergency oil stocks being released by member countries would exceed the 400 million barrels agreed upon in March. Members have pledged to expedite the remaining releases of around 100 million barrels, including over 20 million barrels of diesel, the IEA said. Front-month WTI crude oil futures are down 0.6% at $97.41 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures are 0.4% lower at $105.52 a barrel. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
